name: facial

structure.app/: pages (page.tsx), layouts, loading/error/not-found, API routes (app/api) — universal code
structure.components/: React components — browser-safe; style them with design tokens (var(--aix-*))
structure..aix/design.json: visual identity (style, mood, theme, density, motion)
structure..aix/security.json: security profile (application type, level, requirements) — read before changing code
structure..aix/languages.json: Python pools and every Python declaration (written by aix dev/build)

conventions: Read .aix/security.json first: it defines the security level and requirements every change must respect.
Never import server-only code (agents, tools, workflows, tasks, "aix") from pages or components; use aix/react hooks instead.
Use design tokens (CSS variables --aix-*) instead of hard-coded colors, fonts, radii and spacing.
Agents are private by default; set access: "public" to call them from the browser.
Destructive tools declare capabilities and require approval.
Supported languages: TypeScript, JavaScript and Python (.ts, .js, .py) — nothing else.
TypeScript/JavaScript own the app: pages, layouts, components, API routes, routes.ts, data models (models/), config, security. route() and ui() do not exist in Python.
Python is for AI and data work: tools, agents, workflow steps and background tasks (from aix import tool, agent, workflow, step, task).

Python code never gets database credentials or raw secrets: it calls ctx.db.query/get/count/create/update/delete, ctx.secrets.get (names listed in secrets=[...]), ctx.state, ctx.events.emit and ctx.ai.generate — each needs the matching permissions=[...] (database.read, database.write, state, events, ai).

Data access from Python runs as the user who triggered the call, through the same access rules as TypeScript. Data model types for Python are generated in .aix/schemas/python/aix_models.py (import aix_models).

Call Python from TypeScript by importing the file: import { analyst } from "./agents/analyst.py" (server code only; types come from .aix/schemas). A TS agent can list a Python tool in tools: [...]; a Python agent can list TS tools by name.
Type hints (or Pydantic models) on Python tools are the input/output schema; the host validates both ways. Docstrings are the descriptions models see.
Pools, worker counts, timeouts, limits and Python dependencies: .aix/languages.json and pyproject.toml (+ uv.lock). Declarations are recorded in .aix/languages.json by `aix dev`/`aix build`.
Names are global across languages: a TS and a Python declaration with the same kind and name is an error (the TS one wins).
Styling: Tailwind CSS utilities mapped to the design tokens (bg-surface, text-fg, text-accent …) and plain CSS with var(--aix-*) in app/globals.css; prefer utilities for new code.
